newsitem.title: USA: S&P says to expand worldwide bank coverage.
newsitem.headline: S&P says to expand worldwide bank coverage.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Wednesday it will expand its worldwide coverage of banks by assigning ratings based on public information.

It said the new ratings, identified by a 'pi' subscript, employ analytical procedures that parallel traditional credit ratings but differ in that they are based on public disclosure and other sources of information.

S&P said it will assign about 250 new bank ratings, mostly in emerging markets, during the course of the next year. It said the first series of ratings on banks in Singapore, Indonesia and the Philippines will be announced November 25.
S&P also said it will assign ratings in December on Japanese regional banks and institutions in Mexico, Colombia and Slovakia.

"The 'pi' ratings represent a strong commitment by Standard and Poor's to balance the interests of all market participants," Leo O'Neill, president and chief ratings officer at Standard and Poor's, said in a statement.
"For investors and counterparties, 'pi' ratings provide expanded ratings coverage of financial institutions, using Standard and Poor's well known symbology," he said.

"There is clearly strong capital market interest in the financial instiutions located in emerging markets given their needs for development capital. The 'pi' rating and Standard and Poor's Bank Ratings Service help bridge an information gap in the global banking sector," O'Neill added.

S&P said the analysis will begin with an overview of the economic and industry risk faced by banks operating in a particular country and facets of the business risk faced by a particular bank position will then be taken into account.
The rating agency said financial risk considerations include asset quality, profitability, funding and liquidity, capitalization and risk management.

In addition, the 'pi' ratings are local currency issuer ratings -- opinions of the institutions' overall likelihood of meeting their local currency obligations -- and they will not be modified by plus or minus and will not be put on Creditwatch or have an outlook assigned to them.
It added that the surveillance of 'pi' ratings will occur on an annual basis, although they may be reviewed on an interim basis if events warrant.
